validity.recommendation: No action on existence/classification. Corroborated by 2 genuinely independent lineages beyond the sheet's current petro-news/egy-map (Presidency-portal) citation.
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: real and well-documented. The current cited ref (https://petro-news.com/95212/) does name the pipeline directly ('خط غاز النوبارية – ميت نما') despite the worklist's automated check flagging it (that check searched for the English word 'operating', not the Arabic content, which is present and on-topic - a false-negative in the checker, not a real problem with the source). Independent corroboration beyond that Presidency-portal cluster (petro-news.com and egy-map.com both explicitly source 'من الموقع الرسمي لرئاسة الجمهورية' / the Egyptian Presidency's official projects site, so they are ONE lineage, not two): (1) shbketmsr24.com report on GASCO's official 2015 results, where GASCO chairman Karam Mahmoud names 'خط غاز النوبارية / ميت نما' among GASCO's completed 2015 works feeding the North Giza power station; (2) a World Bank-financed Environmental & Social Impact Assessment, 'Nubaria-Metnama Natural Gas Pipeline, Egypt' (EcoConServ, June 2011, prepared for GASCO/World Bank), which independently describes the same project by the same name, same purpose (feed North Giza power station, strengthen national gas network), same implementer (GASCO). Two independent origins agreeing the pipeline is real -> existence tier=high.
CLASSIFICATION: correct. This is a GASCO national-grid transmission delivery line (feeds a power station intake, part of 'الشبكة القومية للغازات الطبيعية'), not a gathering/plant-internal line, and not oil/NGL. PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas both confirmed by the same sources.
ENDPOINTS: Start=El Noubareya (Beheira) and End=Mit Nema (Al Qalyubia) both confirmed by 2 independent lineages: petro-news/egy-map name both places explicitly, and shbketmsr24 independently also names both ('خط غاز النوبارية / ميت نما ... لتغذية محطة كهرباء شمال الجيزة') - so Location tier=high, independent=true. The pipeline's real function/route (per the WB ESIA) runs El Noubareya area -> North Giza power station intake -> across delta farmland to Mit Nema, i.e. a Beheira->Giza->Qalyubia corridor - consistent with the sheet's StartState/Province=Behara and EndState/Province=Al Qalyubia.

validity.recommendation: Verify LengthKnown against GASCO as-built records. No source found supports the current 66.00 km value (Length [ref] is currently blank in the sheet). The best-corroborated figure is 72 km (34 km 42in Phase 1 + 38 km 32in Phase 2). Do not overwrite without a direct GASCO/as-built confirmation given the WB ESIA complication noted below - flag for human review rather than auto-correct.
validity.researcher_notes:
Length [ref] is currently MISSING_REF and the value 66.00 km has no traceable source. Every source I could find for this project's phase lengths (petro-news.com/95212, egy-map.com project page - both same Presidency-portal lineage) states: Phase 1 = 42in pipe, 34 km, completed Feb 2015; Phase 2 = 32in pipe, 38 km, cost 1.197bn EGP. 34+38 = 72 km, not 66 km. That 72 km figure also matches other web coverage of the same project (multiple outlets repeating the same Phase-1/Phase-2 breakdown). This conflicts with GEM's current 66.00 km by ~8%, and since the current value has zero supporting ref, I did not treat 66 as the default-correct value.
Complication: a 2011 World Bank-financed ESIA for a project also called 'Nubaria-Metnama Natural Gas Pipeline' describes ONE 32-inch segment of this scheme as 105 km long, running from the end of an existing 'Abu Homos-Nubaria 42in pipeline chamber' near Nubaria power station, south along El Rayah El Nasry drain, cutting to North Giza power station, then across delta farmland to link with an already-EXISTING 'El Teena-Metnama 32in pipeline' at Nawa (Ezbet Swelem). That 105 km planning-stage figure for the 32in leg alone does not reconcile with the 38 km Phase-2 figure quoted in the 2015 completion announcements - either the studied route was substantially shortened/rerouted between the 2011 ESIA and 2015 completion, or the 2015 announcements and the ESIA are describing different scopes of a multi-segment scheme (the ESIA explicitly references a separate, already-existing 'El Teena-Metnama 32in' line, which may be GEM's own P3343 El Tina Gas Pipeline, or a different entity again - a related lead worth a follow-up, not resolved here). I am not confident enough in either number to force a value; recommending human review of GASCO's as-built network records rather than blindly substituting 72 km.
Diameter ('32, 42' in) IS well corroborated by the Phase 1/Phase 2 breakdown (42in first phase + 32in second phase matches exactly) and I filled its ref accordingly (see fills). SegmentCost (1,197,000,000 EGP) also matches the Phase 2 cost figure exactly and I filled its ref.
Also flagging a data-quality issue on FuelSource: its current value is a raw egy-map.com URL string, not a named upstream field/facility as the schema requires (FuelSource = upstream field/plant feeding the line, never a fuel type or a bare URL - see docs/reference/gem_schema.md). This looks like a prior data-entry artifact (a ref URL pasted into the value cell). Per schema guidance I did not default it to anything (this line delivers into the national grid via a power-station intake rather than gathering from one named field/facility, so leaving FuelSource blank pending a genuine named source may be the right call, not a fabricated fill).

validity.recommendation: Review Owner1. Both independent sources found name GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company), not 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS), as the entity implementing/owning/operating this line. Recommend changing Owner1 to 'Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO)' (or adding it if the schema distinguishes owner vs operator), pending human confirmation of GASCO's exact corporate/shareholding relationship to EGAS for this asset.
validity.researcher_notes: Owner1 is currently 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' at 100% (=EGAS, the state holding company for the gas sector overall). But the two genuinely independent sources that discuss this project both explicitly attribute it to GASCO, a distinct EGAS/EGPC-owned subsidiary that specifically builds and operates Egypt's national gas transmission trunklines: (1) the World Bank ESIA states plainly, 'The Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO) is taking the responsibility of the implementation of this project, with funding and assistance from the World Bank... The project will be carried out under the supervision and control of GASCO'; (2) shbketmsr24.com's report on the Petroleum Minister's review of GASCO's 2015 results has GASCO's own chairman, Karam Mahmoud, present this exact pipeline ('خط غاز النوبارية / ميت نما') as one of GASCO's own achievements for the year. EGAS may sit above GASCO in Egypt's corporate structure, but for GEM's owner/operator convention (the entity that actually built/owns/runs the physical pipeline asset), GASCO looks like the correct attribution, not the holding company. This is exactly the GASCO-vs-EGAS confusion the SOP calls out for Egypt gas rows.

waypoints.name: North Giza power station (El Kata, Monshaet El Qanater, Giza) - intermediate delivery point per WB ESIA / GASCO 2015 statement

routes.corridor_desc: Per the 2011 World Bank ESIA for this project ('Nubaria-Metnama Natural Gas Pipeline'), the route starts near Nubaria power station in Beheira, runs south along the El Rayah El Nasry drain, cuts east into the North Giza power station intake, then continues across agricultural land in the heart of the Nile Delta (crossing major roads, canals, and the Nile itself via tunneling) before terminating at Nawa/Ezbet Swelem near Mit Nema in Qalyubia. This gives a defensible Beheira -> Giza -> Qalyubia corridor consistent with the sheet's StartState/Province=Behara and EndState/Province=Al Qalyubia. Caveats: the start coordinate given is the general Al Nubaria town centroid (not the specific power-station pipeline chamber the ESIA describes as the true start, which I could not independently pin); the end coordinate is carried over from the sheet's existing RouteNotes Google Maps pin (30.145278,31.234444) - I confirmed independently only that Mit Nema is a village in Qalyub district, Al Qalyubia Governorate (per marefa.org), which is geographically consistent with that pin, but I did not re-derive or independently verify the exact coordinate myself, so it should be read as presumed/plausible rather than freshly sourced.
routes.researcher_notes: Corridor and named waypoints (Nubaria area -> North Giza power station -> Mit Nema/Qalyubia via the delta) are well sourced from the WB ESIA and corroborated by shbketmsr24's independent GASCO statement. Endpoint coordinates are town/facility-level approximations (Al Nubaria centroid; North Giza power plant from globalenergyobservatory.org, not gem.wiki), not survey-grade pipeline chamber locations - I did not fabricate any coordinate; where I lacked independent confirmation (the Mit Nema pin) I explicitly flagged the figure as carried over/presumed rather than freshly verified.

summary: El Noubareya-Mit Nema gas pipeline is real and correctly classified (transmission, feeds North Giza power station), independently confirmed via a World Bank 2011 ESIA and a separate GASCO 2015-results report; flagged concerns: Length=66km has no supporting source (best-sourced figure is 72km = 34+38 phase split, but a WB ESIA complicates this with a 105km planning figure - human review needed) and Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) is likely wrong attribution, should probably be GASCO per both independent sources; filled refs for Diameter, Location, and SegmentCost (all corroborate current values).
